name: HC-SR602 mini PIR motion sensor
description: Miniature passive-infrared motion sensor: OUT goes high (about 3.3 V from the on-board 3.3 V regulator) when a warm body moves within about 5 m (0-3.5 m best) in a 100 degree cone, stays high for about 2.5 s (factory setting, changeable with a chip resistor) and then ignores motion for about 2 s. Draws about 20 uA and runs from 3.3-15 V. Sold as: MH-SR602 (HW-438) mini PIR motion sensor module (round black board with white dome lens, 3-pin header OUT, +, -; unpopulated S+/S- pads for an optional photodiode).
eli5: A tiny heat-motion detector: when a person or animal moves in front of it, it sets its output pin high for a couple of seconds.

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Motion output (marked OUT): about 3.3 V for ~2.5 s per trigger, 0 V otherwise. Safe for 3.3 V GPIOs (end pin 1, next to +).

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3-15 V DC (marked + on the board) (middle pin 2)

supplierQuery: SR602 mini PIR motion sensor module
buildNotes: Header order: OUT, + (VCC), - (GND). Unlike most PIR modules OUT is an END pin and + is in the middle; read the silkscreen before powering.
VCC can be 3.3-15 V (3V3 or 5V both work); the on-board 3.3 V regulator keeps OUT at about 3.3 V, so it connects straight to a GPIO.
OUT is active high: 1 for about 2.5 s after motion, then a ~2 s blocking time in which it ignores motion. Longer hold times need a different chip resistor.
The two S+/S- holes are for an optional photodiode (night-only operation); leave them empty for normal use.
Give it up to a minute after power-up to settle before trusting the output.

driver.code:
# HC-SR602 (MH-SR602 / HW-438) mini PIR motion sensor module, MicroPython driver.
# The module carries a digital PIR detector and a 3.3 V LDO, so OUT is a logic output
# from the 3.3 V rail even when "+" is fed 5-15 V:
#   HIGH (about 3.3 V) for about 2.5 s after motion (factory delay; set by a chip resistor),
#   re-triggering while motion continues.
#   LOW (0 V) otherwise; after going low it ignores motion for about 2 s (blocking time).
# OUT connects straight to a 3.3 V GPIO. No pull-up/down is needed.
# Supply 3.3-15 V DC on "+"; quiescent current about 20 uA.
from machine import Pin


class HCSR602:
    def __init__(self, out_pin):
        self.pin = Pin(out_pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(out_pin, int) else out_pin

    def motion(self):
        """True while the sensor reports motion (OUT high)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 1

    def on_change(self, handler):
        """Call handler(motion: bool) on every edge of OUT. Pass None to stop."""
        if handler is None:
            self.pin.irq(handler=None)
            return
        self.pin.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING | Pin.IRQ_FALLING,
                     handler=lambda p: handler(p.value() == 1))

example.code:
from hc_sr602 import HCSR602
import time

pir = HCSR602({OUT})
while True:
    print('MOTION=%d' % pir.motion())
    time.sleep(0.5)
